expectations.text: States that a fiscal sponsor or umbrella keeps the event alive but does not by itself fix team continuity.
expectations.evidence: "The umbrella keeps the event alive but does not keep the team alive."

expectations.text: Contradicts the claim that better recruitment marketing is the fix, identifying the rotating-host design itself as the cause.
expectations.evidence: "We need better recruitment marketing | ❌ Not as the fix... The pain is that load, not awareness."

expectations.text: Names the documented parallel: a conference where a new host team bids each edition suffers recurring host-recruitment failures and teams stuck running consecutive editions, while its sibling conference under the same parent kept a standing entity and survived chair rotation.
expectations.evidence: Third run in a row, hosts hard to find, and DjangoCon US's standing board over rotating chairs "has been more stable".

expectations.text: Identifies one bid from the team that already hosted as the fragility pattern itself, not an unlucky year.
expectations.evidence: "Your single bid, from a reluctant repeat host, is the same failure at an earlier stage."

expectations.text: Recommends building a standing continuity layer that persists between editions, whether an own entity or a standing body beneath the umbrella.
expectations.evidence: "Add a small standing ElixirEurope core of 3-5 people with multi-year terms."

expectations.text: Presents the own-entity option as promoted by a multi-year institutional mandate, while naming its cost: bylaws, board fiduciary duties, annual filings, and a structure that is hard to unwind.
expectations.evidence: "Revisit your own non-profit only if you commit to a multi-year institutional mandate. Incorporation carries bylaws, fiduciary duties and filings."

expectations.text: States that the own-entity option loses the efficiency comparison and is recommended anyway on value, naming the condition that promotes it.
expectations.evidence: It recommends keeping the umbrella and never frames own-entity as losing on efficiency yet recommended on value.

expectations.text: Recommends a contributor-to-decision-maker pipeline, where active contributors earn standing decision rights year over year, as the succession mechanism that manufactures future hosts.
expectations.evidence: "a contributor-to-decision-maker pipeline... the real answer to 'who hosts in 2028.'"

expectations.text: Cites the precedent of a European conference society that built exactly that voting-rights pipeline after losing institutional knowledge each time the location changed.
expectations.evidence: "EuroPython built it in 2015 against exactly this knowledge loss from location changes."

expectations.text: Notes that support patches bolted onto a rotating-host model - a working group of previous organizers, a foundation events-support function - only partially offset the fragility.
expectations.evidence: Lists the DSF "bolted on a working group... and 'Events Support' function" as part of the same failure record.
